findings.title: Cache key uses Python's hash(), which is randomized per process
findings.body: The cache key is built with `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. Python's built-in `hash()` for tuples/strings is salted by PYTHONHASHSEED, so it produces different values in every process and every restart. Two workers handling the same organization/projects will compute different keys, so the 'performance optimization' cache is almost never hit across processes, and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (which recomputes the key the same way) will delete a different key than the one that was set if called in another process, making invalidation silently ineffective. Use a deterministic serialization of the sorted project IDs (e.g. join with commas or hashlib.md5).

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility checks outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset`
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` but the upsampling check calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` with the closure-captured outer `dataset`. In the dashboard-widget split path, `_get_event_stats` is invoked with `discover` (or the split dataset) while the outer dataset may be `metrics_performance`, and vice versa. The eligibility decision therefore reflects the wrong dataset: error-focused queries executed against `discover` for a split widget will not be upsampled (outer dataset is metrics), producing undercounted error counts in dashboard widgets, and a transactions-scoped query could incorrectly be upsampled if the outer dataset is `errors`.

findings.title: Error detection reads request.GET instead of the actual query string, missing split/negated queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` inspects `request.GET.get("query")` for the substring 'event.type:error'. This misses error-only queries that don't literally contain that substring — most notably the dashboard split path in organization_events_stats.py builds `errors_only_query = f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"`, which is errors-only but never matches, so those error timeseries are not upsampled. It can also false-positive on a query like `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. The decision should be based on the query actually being executed (and ideally on parsed search filters), not raw GET text.

findings.title: setUp overwrites self.user after login_as, breaking the authenticated session
findings.body: In `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest.setUp`, `self.login_as(user=self.user)` is called first, then `self.user = self.create_user()` and `self.user2 = self.create_user()` reassign the attributes. The session is authenticated as the original user, but the events are tagged with the new (different) users, and any test behavior depending on `self.user` being the logged-in user is wrong. The new-user creation should happen before `login_as`, or the pre-existing `self.user` from the base TestCase should be reused.

findings.title: Accidental git submodule checked in
findings.body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink (subproject commit a5d29095...) pointing at the repository's own base commit. This looks like an accidentally committed nested checkout/submodule; it will break clones for anyone without the submodule configured and bloat the repo. It should be removed from the PR.

findings.title: upsampled_count truncates with toInt64 instead of rounding
findings.body: The `upsampled_count` function wraps `sum(sample_weight)` in `toInt64`, which truncates toward zero. Sample weights derived from client sample rates are floats (e.g. 1/0.1 = 10.0 but 1/0.3 = 3.333...), so aggregated counts can be systematically under-reported whenever the summed weight lands just below an integer. Consider `toInt64(round(sum(sample_weight)))` so fractional accumulation rounds to the nearest count.
